rows.name: protected_copper_preserved
rows.why: all 255 segment(s) on ANT_FEED, NFC1, NFC2 came back, each within 55 nm of where it was sent — under the 100 nm the format can carry (halo_rev_a.filtered.ses: (resolution um 10) = one step is 0.0001 mm). 25 segment(s) ADDED on those nets ({'ANT_FEED': 2, 'NFC1': 5, 'NFC2': 18}) — the router extending a protected net to reach its pads, which is routing, not rerouting

rows.name: protected_length_preserved
rows.why: the matched conductor is 162.2479 mm going out and 162.2480 mm coming back, a difference of 57 nm against a quantisation budget of 51000 nm (two grid steps per segment). The NFC coil's inductance and the element's resonance are both functions of this length

rows.name: antenna_arm_not_shadowed
rows.why: the closest foreign copper to the 2.4 GHz arm (37 segment(s) at 0.6 mm; 2 further ANT_FEED segment(s) are the feed run and are NOT the radiator), IN PLAN VIEW ACROSS ALL LAYERS, is 0.3627 mm — net NFC1 on B.Cu at (22.857, 8.718). Floor is 0.3 mm: lane T3, 2026-09-05: the Ø25.2 mm coil at a 0.30 mm gap solves to 2.4321 GHz in band; the same coil under the arm solves to 1.7666 GHz, a 668 MHz shift that is not recoverable by tuning
